title: What Antioxidants Do to Your Body

cards.prompt: Explain like I'm 10: what is a free radical?
cards.answer: Electrons like to be in pairs. A free radical has a lonely electron with no partner, so it steals one from whatever it bumps into, like a protein or DNA.

cards.prompt: Antioxidants stop the chain reaction by donating an ____ to the unpaired one.
Free radicals are entirely bad for the body.
cards.answer: Myth: our immune system uses free radicals to kill pathogens.

cards.prompt: Order the chain reaction of free radical damage.
items: A free radical with an unpaired electron bumps into a molecule
It steals an electron from it
The victim molecule is left unpaired and steals again
Antioxidant donates an electron to stop the chain
cards.answer: Stealing spreads from molecule to molecule until an antioxidant donates an electron.

cards.prompt: Which is NOT an antioxidant or antioxidant source?
cards.answer: Free radicals are what antioxidants neutralize; the others are antioxidants or sources.

cards.prompt: A friend says the body only gets antioxidants from fruit. What do you reply?
cards.answer: The body also makes its own, like glutathione and enzymes, besides food sources such as vitamins C and E, selenium, zinc and carotenoids.
